To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the statistical error is smallest for monthly mean 5° zonal mean RO climatologies with at least 1000 measurements per bin, (2) the sampling error can be reduced to 30% or less by subtracting it from the climatological data, (3) the systematic error is generally the largest error component and (4) the systematic error can be significantly reduced by using physical atmospheric parameters instead of the more commonly used dry atmospheric parameters.

the statistical error is the smallest error component in monthly mean 10 degree zonal mean climatology, the sampling error increases roughly linear with increasing latitude and is smallest at low latitudinal regions, the residual sampling error after subtraction of the sampling error is estimated to be less than 30% of its original value, the systematic error accounts for the largest part of the total error, and the total climatologic error is estimated to less than 0.15% in refractivity at low latitudes

the statistical error can be reduced to less than 0.01% in refractivity by using more than 600 RO profiles per 10° zonally averaged bin, the residual sampling error can be reduced below 0.02% in refractivity, and the systematic error can be reduced from about 0.07 to 0.05% in refractivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantification of the uncertainty in RO climatological fields.
the quantification of uncertainty in climatologies derived from GPS RO measurements.
the question of how to quantify the uncertainty of climatological fields based on GPS radio occultation data, which is an important prerequisite for the use of these fields in climate research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RO climatological data sets are highly suitable for the derivation of climate statistics and trends in climate variables.
RO climatologies of dry parameters can be used for a wide range of applications, but for climate research it is recommended to subtract the sampling errors.

RO climatologies of dry parameters are highly suitable for climatic studies and that the error model presented in this study is a valuable tool for the analysis and interpretation of such climatologies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RO measurements are highly suitable for climatological studies, and the error model presented here can be used to assess the quality of RO-based climatological fields.
the RO technique provides a highly accurate tool to study the dry atmosphere and that RO measurements are highly valuable to study climate processes.
RO measurements can be used to derive reliable climatologies of dry atmospheric parameters with an accuracy of about 0.1 K in temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RO data are suitable for climate research and can be used to derive high-quality climatological fields, provided the errors in these fields are accounted for properly.
RO climatologies provide a highly valuable data set for climate research.
the total RO climatological error can be estimated with an analytical error model that can be easily applied to RO data from different satellite missions.
